title: Store: reject non-array property values at compile time in `upsert()`
body:
## Changelog Entry

<!-- To be added via `node ./scripts/changelog/new.mjs` once the PR number is known. -->

## Description

`nodeSchema` cast its rest schema to `BaseSchema<unknown, …>` (`Node.ts:41`), so every non-named property on `Node` was typed as `unknown`. Invalid values compiled and were only rejected at runtime:

```ts
controller.edit(transaction =>
  transaction.upsert('_:m-1', () => ({
    '@id': '_:m-1',
    '@type': new Set(['Message']),
    text: 'Hello' // Compiled, but `text` must be `PropertyValue` (an array), e.g. ['Hello']
  }))
);
```

This change makes that line a compile-time error.

## Design

TypeScript has no way to say "every property except `@id`/`@type`/… must be `X`". The index signature that `objectWithRest` produces also applies to the named properties, so no object literal can be assigned to the uncast `Node`, including valid ones.

The type is therefore split into one for reading and one for writing:

- **`Node`** (reading): the real `InferOutput` of `nodeSchema`. Named properties keep their types and every other property is `PropertyValue`. Object literals can't be assigned to it.
- **`NodeInit<T>`** (writing): a generic check over the inferred literal type `T`.
   - Named properties must match their schema types, and the required ones must be present.
   - Every other key must be `PropertyValue`.

`upsert()` now validates the updater's return value through `NodeInit<T>`:

```ts
upsert<T>(id: Identifier, updater: (node: Node | undefined) => NodeInit<T>): void;
```

This covers both new literals and spreads of an existing node (`{ ...node, text: 'Hello' }`). Runtime validation by `nodeSchema` is unchanged.

`Node` is not exported from the package. The only public-facing change is the generic `upsert()` signature.

## Specific Changes

- **`node/Node.ts`**
   - Removed the `unknown` cast. The rest properties of `Node` are now typed as `PropertyValue`.
   - Moved the named properties into `namedPropertiesSchema` and reused its `.entries` in `objectWithRest`.
   - Added and exported `NodeInit<T>`.
- **`Store.ts`**: `StoreTransaction.upsert()` and its implementation are now generic over `NodeInit<T>`.
- **`private/createNode.ts`**
   - With the stricter types, the `instanceof Set` check no longer narrowed enough to compile.
   - `hasPart`/`isPartOf` are now read from the parsed node instead. Behavior is the same.
- **`benchmark.ts`**: dropped the `: Node` return type on `createMessage()`, because it builds a literal.
- **`Store.test.ts`**
   - Added a test where a new node has `text: 'Hello, World!'`. It asserts the compile-time error (`@ts-expect-error`) and the runtime throw.
   - In the existing `position: 1` test, replaced the `as unknown as Node` cast with `@ts-expect-error`.
   - Marked two existing JSON-literal tests with `@ts-expect-error`. They pass invalid `@value`s on purpose (a recursive object, and an object containing `Date`), which the old typing silently accepted.

- [x] I have added tests and executed them locally
- [ ] I have added `.changelog/<PR#>-<slug>.md`
- [ ] I have updated documentation
